abomination-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Abomination is a monstrous gamma-powered villain created after deliberately exposing himself to a radiation blast meant to replicate the Hulk’s transformation. Instead, the dose turned him into a reptilian powerhouse.
abomination-reading-order.text: Abomination is a monstrous gamma-powered villain created after deliberately exposing himself to a radiation blast meant to replicate the Hulk’s transformation. Instead, the dose turned him into a reptilian powerhouse.

adam-warlock-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Adam Warlock is a powerful artificial being created to be the perfect human by a group of Earth scientists known as the Enclave. Though noble, he struggles with his darker counterpart, Magus, representing the corruption of his potential. Adam Warlock stands as both savior and threat to the cosmos.

agatha-harkness-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Agatha Harkness is one of Earth’s oldest and most powerful witches, possessing centuries of knowledge in the mystic arts. Mentor, manipulator, and occasional ally, she has guided heroes such as the Fantastic Four and Scarlet Witch. Her motives are rarely clear, but her mastery of magic makes her a formidable force.

agents-of-atlas-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: In 1958 Yellow Claw kidnapped President Eisenhower. Authorized to assemble a special rescue team, FBI Agent Jimmy Woo selected a roster that came to him in a dream: Gorilla Man, Venus, Marvel Boy and Namora.

alpha-flight-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Alpha Flight is Canada’s premier superhuman defense team, operating under federal mandate to protect national and global security. Core members include Guardian, a technologically enhanced leader; Sasquatch, a gamma-powered powerhouse; Shaman and Snowbird, wielders of Indigenous and Arctic mysticism; and Northstar and Aurora, mutant speedsters and light manipulators.

anya-corazon-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Anya is a teenage girl from Brooklyn. Fatally injured by a fight between the Sisterhood of the Wasps and the Spider Society, the Spider Society’s sorcerer was forced to transfer some of his power to her to save her life. After the transfer she received a spider-shaped tattoo which gave her enhanced strength and agility. Originally using the alias Araña, she has since started using the Spider-Girl name.

apocalypse-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Born 5000 years ago Apocalypse, born En Sabah Nur, is one of the first mutants. Apocalypse is a supervillain antagonist of the X-Men. Obsessed with the concept of ‘survival of the fittest’ he has conducted numerous experiments in its pursuit.

arcade-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Arcade affects a manner of dress and speech that makes him appear to be a comedic character. His preferred method of murder is an underground funhouse of colorful deathtraps, which he has dubbed “Murderworld.”

avengers-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock:
The Avengers are Earth’s mightiest heroes,  formed to fight the foes no single hero could withstand.  The Avengers are the most prestigious and powerful super-hero team in the world,  an ever-shifting assemblage of super-beings,  adventurers and crime fighters devoted to protecting the planet from menaces beyond the scope of conventional authorities.

Their success has resulted in various splinter-teams and spin-off teams,  both nationwide and worldwide,  with different members

baron-zemo-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Helmut Zemo is the 13th Baron Zemo. His father taught him the idea that the Master Race should rule the world. Helmut would ultimately follow in his father’s footsteps as a supervillain using his family’s money and his own scientific know-how to recreate his father’s work.

beta-ray-bill-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Beta Ray Bill is one of the few individuals worthy of wielding Mjolnir. After an initial rivalry with Thor for possession of the weapon, the alien warrior was granted a hammer of his own, called Stormbreaker, and the two reconciled as staunch allies.

black-bolt-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Black Bolt is the ruler of the Inhumans, a reclusive race of genetically altered superhumans. His most devastating weapon is his voice. A whisper can level a city, cause distant volcanoes to become active, and generate tremors on the far side of the planet.

black-widow-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Natasha Romanova was originally a Russian spy, an enemy of Iron Man. Eventually she defected to the United States, becoming an agent of S.H.I.E.L.D., and a member of the Avengers.

blade-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Blade was born over seven decades ago. During his birth a vampire feasted on his mother, passing on a series of enzymes that altered her baby. Blade grew up with a hatred for vampires and became a vampire hunter.

blink-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock:
In the primary Earth-616 continuity, Blink was tense, panicky and frightened of her powers and could not control them.

The Age of Apocalypse continuity Blink showed a more refined power set and has mastered several methods of utilizing her powers.

bullseye-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: A psychopathic assassin, Bullseye uses the opportunities afforded by his line of work to exercise his homicidal tendencies and to work out his own personal vendetta against Daredevil.
bullseye-reading-order.text: A psychopathic assassin, Bullseye uses the opportunities afforded by his line of work to exercise his homicidal tendencies and to work out his own personal vendetta against Daredevil.

cable-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Nathan Summers was born to Cyclops and Madelyne Pryor, a clone of Jean Grey. As a child he was infected with the Techno-Organic Virus and taken to the future in the hopes of finding a cure. Eventually he returned as a grown man, Cable, and existed at the same time as his infant self.

carnage-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Carnage is a homicidal symbiote bonded to Cletus Kasady, a sadistic serial killer. Spawned from Venom, Carnage is stronger, faster, and far more ruthless, driven by pure chaos and bloodlust. With no sense of restraint and a twisted philosophy that worships carnage itself, he is one of Spider-Man and Venom’s most terrifying enemies.

carol-danvers-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: After encountering the Kree hero Captain Marvel, Carol Danvers was accidentally subjected to radiation that transformed her into a superhuman warrior, calling herself Ms. Marvel. Carol has now adopted the mantle of Captain Marvel for herself.

cloak-and-dagger-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Tyrone Johnson (Cloak) and Tandy Bowen (Dagger) met in New York City as runaways. The two teens were forcibly delivered to a criminal chemist who was developing a new synthetic heroin, testing it on runaway teens with fatal results. Johnson and Bowen somehow survived injections of the drug, and fled. During their escape, the drug turned them into superpowered beings.

cyclops-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Cyclops can emit powerful beams of energy from his eyes and cannot control the beams without the aid of special eyewear. He was a founding member of the X-Men and soon became the team’s field leader.

daisy-johnson-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Daisy Johnson, a.k.a. Quake, is a superhuman with seismic powers. Taken in by S.H.I.E.L.D., she was offered the chance to be properly trained in the use of her powers in exchange for loyalty to Nick Fury.

daken-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Daken, is the mutant son of Wolverine and a complex antihero shaped by pain, manipulation, and vengeance. Unpredictable, charismatic, and deadly, he has served on teams like Dark Avengers and X-Factor, walking a razor’s edge between villainy and reluctant heroism in the shadow of his infamous father.

doctor-doom-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Doctor Doom is the leader of the nation of Latveria, which he rules in a dictatorship. He is both a genius inventor and a powerful sorcerer. Over the years he has been the nemesis of the Fantastic Four and also fought Iron Man, the Avengers, and other superheroes.

doctor-octopus-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: A highly intelligent mad scientist, Otto Octavius is one of Spider-Man’s greatest enemies. Eventually becoming terminally ill, Doctor Octopus was able to transfer his mind into Peter Parker’s body, becoming the Superior Spider-Man.

doop-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Doop is a green, floating spheroid creature of unknown origins who speaks in his own language. Doop is also a good videographer. Doop’s teammates have an unfortunate tendency to die.

dormammu-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Dormammu is one of the most powerful mystical entities in the Marvel Universe. It is unknown exactly how ancient he is, as he inhabits a wholly alien realm, separate from the rest of the Marvel Universe, that defies the laws of physics as understood on Earth.

echo-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Echo, real name Maya Lopez, is a deaf Native American superhero with the extraordinary ability of photographic reflexes, she can perfectly mimic any physical movement or fighting style she sees.

ego-the-living-planet-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Ego originated like any other planet, coalescing over millions of years from cosmic gases and dust. But unlike any other known planet, Ego developed consciousness and intelligence.

elektra-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Elektra is a ninja assassin of Greek descent, who wields a pair of bladed sai as her trademark weapon. Elektra is a love interest of Daredevil, but her violent nature and mercenary lifestyle divide the two.

elsa-bloodstone-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Elsa Bloodstone is a fearless monster hunter and the daughter of legendary immortal warrior Ulysses Bloodstone. Armed with both modern firearms and ancient weaponry, she’s as witty and sarcastic as she is deadly.

eternals-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: The Eternals are an offshoot of humanity which were created one million years ago by the enigmatic alien Celestials to defend Earth with their superhuman powers and abilities. Their primary adversaries are the Deviants, who share a similar origin and pose a regular threat to humanity. Due to their virtual immortality, Eternals have largely secluded themselves from humans, with their god-like status forming the basis of various mythological figures around the world.

galactus-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Galactus is the Devourer of Worlds, a cosmic constant as old as the universe itself. Once the mortal Galan of Taa, he survived the previous universe’s collapse and was reborn during the Big Bang as a being of unfathomable power.

Gambit is also incredibly skilled in card-throwing, hand-to-hand combat, and the use of a staff. Gambit is known to charge playing cards and other objects with kinetic energy, using them as explosive projectiles.

ghost-rider-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Stunt motorcyclist Johnny Blaze, in order to save the life of his father, agreed to give his soul to Mephisto. At night and when around evil, Blaze finds his flesh consumed by hellfire, causing his head to become a flaming skull. He rides a fiery motorcycle and wields trademark blasts of hellfire from his skeletal hands.

guardians-of-the-galaxy-1969-reading-ord.originalHtmlBlock:
In the 31st century the Badoon have conquered the solar system. Four survivors decide to band together to rid the Earth and its colonies from Badoon oppression. They named themselves the Guardians of the Galaxy, becoming a force committed to resist the Badoon occupation of the galaxy.

You can find a reading order for the modern Guardians of the Galaxy team here: Guardians of the Galaxy (2008).

guardians-of-the-galaxy-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: In the aftermath of the Phalanx invasion of the Kree, Star-Lord decides to form a team of interstellar heroes that will be proactive in protecting the galaxy, rather than reacting to crises as they happen. On the recommendation of Nova, the group establishes a base of operations on the space station Knowhere, which possesses a teleportation system with near-universal range.

hawkeye-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Hawkeye is an Avenger without powers. To those who’ve fought beside him, he’s the man who never blinks when the odds turn fatal. Clint Barton stands between gods and civilians, arrow drawn, trusting skill and nerve to bridge the gap.

hercules-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Hercules is the son of Zeus, king of the Olympian gods. He is a founding member of The Champions. After being exiled from Olympus by Zeus the Avengers housed Hercules as their guest for months, and he often assisted them in their adventures. He was eventually made an official member of the team.

He developed technology to accelerate genetic mutation, creating entire species such as the New Men, animal-human hybrids. Operating from his space-faring base, Counter-Earth, the High Evolutionary often acts as both a godlike creator and a dangerous manipulator.

hope-summers-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Hope is the first mutant to be born since M-Day. After several fights over possession of the baby Cyclops decides it would be better off with Cable, and allows him to take her to the future.

howard-the-duck-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Howard the Duck was hatched on Duckworld, a planet in another universe, where intelligent life evolved from waterfowl. Duckworld resembles mankind’s Earth in an astounding number of ways, including the fact that ducks speak English.

inhumans-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: At the beginning of the Kree-Skrull War, millions of years ago, the alien Kree established a station on the planet Uranus. They discovered that sentient life on nearby Earth had genetic potential invested in it by the alien Celestials. The Kree began to experiment on Earth’s then-primitive Homo sapiens to produce the genetically advanced Inhuman race. Although their experiments were successful in creating a strain of humanity with extraordinary abilities, the Kree abandoned their experiment. The Inhumans went on to form a society of their own, which thrived in seclusion from the rest of humanity and developed advanced technology.

Her family was killed and Jessica spent several months in a coma. She was placed in an orphanage and adopted by the Jones family. Jessica later discovered that her radiation exposure granted her super strength, limited invulnerability, and flight.

With his new abilities and dispassionate outlook, Essex took the new name, “Sinister”.

the-maker-reading-order.text: The Maker is a twisted, hyper-intelligent version of Reed Richards from a destroyed universe. Once a hero, his mind fractured after witnessing the collapse of his world, transforming him into a cold, calculating manipulator.

the-mandarin-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: The Mandarin is one of Iron Man’s most formidable enemies; a warlord, genius tactician, and master martial artist empowered by ten alien rings of immense power.
the-mandarin-reading-order.text: The Mandarin is one of Iron Man’s most formidable enemies; a warlord, genius tactician, and master martial artist empowered by ten alien rings of immense power.

the-sentry-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Middle aged, overweight Bob Reynolds remembers that he is The Sentry, a superhero whose "power of one million exploding suns" derives from a special serum. Realizing that his archenemy the Void is returning, Reynolds seeks out several prominent Marvel characters to warn them and to discover why no one remembers The Sentry.

thunderbolts-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: The Thunderbolts are a team of reformed supervillains originally assembled by Baron Zemo. Initially a ploy for power, some members genuinely embraced redemption, leading the team to evolve over time. Various incarnations have included both villains and heroes, with leaders like Hawkeye, Norman Osborn, and Winter Soldier guiding the group.

tigra-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Tigra, real name Greer Nelson, is a feline-themed superheroine who gained her powers through a mystical transformation by the Cat People. Gifted with superhuman agility, heightened senses, retractable claws, and a mystical bond to her feline heritage, she balances her human intellect with animal instincts.

ultron-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Ultron is an advanced artificial intelligence created by Dr. Hank Pym to bring peace to humanity, only to conclude that extermination is the best path to order. Ultron’s intellect rivals the greatest minds, making him one of the Avengers’ most relentless foes. Though destroyed many times, he always returns, proving that as long as technology endures, so too will Ultron’s cold, merciless will.

vision-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: The Vision is a synthezoid created by Ultron to destroy the Avengers but who ultimately rebelled against him and joined the Avengers.

war-machine-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: James “Rhodey” Rhodes is a friend of Tony Stark, who sometimes assumed the mantle of Iron Man when Tony was unable to. Eventually he was given his own suit of powered armor and operates under the name War Machine.

winter-soldier-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: The Winter Soldier is a legendary covert operative feared across the globe. Once believed dead, Bucky Barnes was captured, brainwashed, and transformed into an elite assassin, carrying out impossible missions for decades.

wonder-man-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: Wonder Man, born Simon Williams, is a former corporate magnate transformed into a superhuman by ionic energy. Initially created as a pawn against the Avengers, Simon’s conscience led him to join the team, balancing his powers with a deep moral compass.

x-23-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: X-23 is a female clone of Wolverine. Like Wolverine, X-23 has a regenerative healing factor, superhuman stamina, senses, speed, agility, and reflexes. She also has retractable adamantium-coated bone claws in her hands and feet. X-23 was created to be the perfect killing machine.

x-factor-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: The X-Factor name has been used by multiple teams. The original X-Factor posed as mutant hunters while secretly helping mutants. The second team was a government-sponsored mutant superhero team. The third team was X-Factor Investigations, a detective agency. Currently the name X-Factor is used for a corporate-sponsored superhero team.

x-force-reading-order.originalHtmlBlock: An offshoot of the X-Men, X-Force takes a more militant and aggressive approach towards its enemies compared to the X-Men. X-Force was involved in attacks on mutant groups such as the Mutant Liberation Front and was itself branded early in its career as a group of terrorists.
